Incorporating the Financial Stability Report (FSR) insights shifts the balance of risks more to the downside than the literature-only view. The FSR (Nov 2019 and April 2020) flagged elevated pre-pandemic vulnerabilities—high corporate leverage, valuation pressures, and significant funding risks in nonbank intermediation (for example, prime MMFs and bond funds), alongside Treasury market fragilities that materialized in March 2020. These factors amplified the COVID shock and increased tail risks, even as banks generally entered with strong capital and liquidity. While the Fed’s move to the effective lower bound, large-scale Treasury and agency MBS purchases, expanded repo operations, discount window actions, and coordinated dollar liquidity swap lines helped restore market functioning and support credit flow, the FSR’s assessment of heightened vulnerabilities implies a more negative overall tone for the outlook and financial conditions than a macro-only read.
